title: RTS + FPS hybrid game in progress
author: lemonlemons
selftext: Some gameplay of a game I have been working on last couple days. Two of my favorite genres combined, going for retro futuristic style. All done with Claude Code using Opus 5.5.

comments.author: Almaravarion
comments.body:
Interesting design, though frankly I wonder how do You intend to marry gameplay that is designed around multiple, cheap and replaceable units (or even - cannon fodder units) like C&C, with first person design that seems to favour more unique, specialized, high value units (more like commando units)?

I wonder if using different basegame, maybe one in which units are less numerous, with maybe RPG elements (Original War comes to mind) wouldn't work better, where even base game style rotated around specialists, rather than 'bulk bodyparts'.

comments.author: Sword_Dev
comments.body:
I really like your design, but there’s one problem you probably have to think about. RTS is all about map awareness and APM, while in FPS your ability to gather information on a big map is really limited. So I don’t think RTS and FPS can be properly combined in a competitive setting.

If you want it to be competitive, I’d suggest a dedicated commander role that a player is locked into, playing the RTS side in first person. That’s the only way I can see it being somewhat fair. Otherwise pure RTS players will pretty much stomp the FPS players. And if you give FPS players big buffs to compensate, classic RTS players probably won’t play it at all. A lot of RTS fans are hardcore mouse-and-keyboard players.

comments.author: Maple-Syrup89
comments.body:
This looks technically really great! 

How is the game balance given that FPS is almost never as efficient as RTS in terms of actually winning battles? 

Do you give an advantage to player controlled damage?

replies.author: lemonlemons
replies.body:
Balancing definetily needs work. I am big fan of classic rts but it felt boring doing straight clone of Dune 2, C&C etc.

At the moment, fps doesn’t give extra benefit but I do have engineer type units and saboteur type units that can hijack and destroy enemy buildings, as well as snipe enemy infantry and plant explosives in enemy vehicles.

My initial idea was that fps player could sneak and destroy enemy base more easily than rts player as fps player has full freedom for real time movement, creating interesting mechanic compared to traditional rts gameplay. I was also thinking that if there was squad of skilled fps players, they could beat rts player by pure skill in battle as well. But needs testing for sure.
